issues.title: [BUG] apm install from a git hook writes into the invoking repo (GIT_DIR beats -C), detaching its HEAD
issues.body:
## What happens

If you run `apm install` from a git hook, apm can write into the repo that invoked it. In our case it dumped a dependency's whole history into our object store and left our HEAD detached on that dependency's code. Took out a worktree, and it's bitten us a few times over the last couple months before we tracked it down.

The trigger is `GIT_DIR`. git exports it to hooks, and in a linked worktree it's an absolute path, so it follows every child process around. apm shells out to git, those children inherit it, and they stop caring where apm meant to point them.

## Why `-C` doesn't save you

I think this is the core of it. `-C` only changes directory, and `GIT_DIR` overrides directory based repo discovery, so `GIT_DIR` wins. Small standalone repro, no apm involved:

```
$ GIT_DIR=repoA/.git git -C repoB fetch <src> <sha>
repoA: gets the objects and FETCH_HEAD
repoB: gets nothing at all
```

So `git -C <cache-db> fetch ...` in `apm install` isn't actually scoped to the cache db when `GIT_DIR` is set.

## How that turns into a detached HEAD

The two problems feed each other:

1. The cache fetch gets redirected into the hooking repo, so apm's cache db stays empty.
2. Because the db is empty, the cache checkout fails with `fatal: unable to read tree`.
3. That falls back to the `apm_modules` path, which runs a bare `git checkout <sha>` with no `-C` and no `--git-dir` at all.
4. That checkout gets redirected too. And the objects are already sitting in the hooking repo from step 1, so it succeeds, and detaches that repo's HEAD onto the dependency.

Here's the `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT` capture, trimmed to the git children:

```
git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -C ~/Library/Caches/apm/git/db_v1/<hash> fetch https://github.com/github/gh-stack <sha>
  git index-pack --stdin --fix-thin --keep=fetch-pack ... --pack_header=2,1534
git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null clone --local --shared --no-checkout <db> <checkouts_v1 path>
git config --get-regexp ^url\..*\.insteadof$
git clone -v -- https://github.com/github/gh-stack.git <repo>/apm_modules/github/gh-stack
git checkout 2bd699a544a09cb5c45a013d03416e0894b0454e
git remote get-url origin
```

That bare `git checkout` on the second to last line is the one that does the damage.

## Repro

apm 0.28.0, macOS, git 2.x from Xcode.

1. Make a repo and add a linked worktree: `git worktree add ../wt -b wt`. The linked worktree matters, that's what makes `GIT_DIR` absolute. A primary checkout gets a relative `.git` and it's harmless.
2. In the worktree, `apm.yml` with one **unpinned** git dep:
   ```yaml
   name: repro
   version: 0.0.0
   targets: [claude]
   dependencies:
     apm:
       - github/gh-stack
     mcp: []
   ```
3. Cold the cache so a real fetch has to happen: empty out `objects/pack/` in that dep's `~/Library/Caches/apm/git/db_v1/<hash>` and delete its `checkouts_v1/<hash>` dir.
4. `GIT_DIR=$(git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir) apm install`

What you get:

| | HEAD | foreign packs in your repo | skill installed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GIT_DIR` inherited | detached on the dep's commit | 3 files, 1534 objects | yes |
| `env -u GIT_DIR ...` | on its branch, untouched | 0 | yes |

A warm complete cache hides all of this, since there's no fetch. That's why it took us so long to pin down, we kept failing to reproduce it.

Unpinned deps make it way more likely, since apm re-resolves the moving ref every install and fetches again. The dep that kept getting us was the only one in our `apm.yml` without a `#sha`.

## Two things that made this really hard to diagnose

Not asking you to fix these, but they might help whoever picks this up:

- The reflog blames the wrong command. `git merge` exports `GIT_REFLOG_ACTION="merge origin/main"`, and apm's checkout inherits the label, so our reflog showed a merge nobody ran. In a clean repro with no such env it correctly reads `checkout: moving from wt to <sha>`.
- `git remote get-url origin` still reads correct the whole time, so we spent weeks thinking something was rewriting our remote.

## Suggested fix

Two separate things:

1. Use `--git-dir` (or `-C` plus explicitly clearing the env) instead of relying on `-C`, since `GIT_DIR` beats it.
2. Don't run a bare `git checkout` in the `apm_modules` fallback. It has no scoping at all, so it lands wherever the ambient env points.

Clearing git's repo-locating env before shelling out would cover both: `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, `GIT_NAMESPACE`.

We worked around it on our side by wrapping the call in `env -u` for those vars, which fixes it for us. But anyone running `apm install` from a hook is exposed, and it's a pretty rough failure when it hits.

Might be adjacent to #2436 and #2713, which are also apm getting confused by worktrees, though the mechanism here is different.

issues.title: [BUG] Conforming Claude Code plugin rejected: schema-bearing .claude-plugin/plugin.json never reaches the legacy path
issues.body:
## Summary `apm install` refuses any Claude Code plugin whose `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` carries the official Claude Code `$schema`. The manifest is valid for Claude Code, and the identical package installs cleanly once the `$schema` line is deleted. The rejection comes from a root-manifest router being reused as a predicate on the legacy manifest, where it raises instead of returning. ## Reproduction Three files, no network: ```bash mkdir -p plug/.claude-plugin consumer printf -- '---\nname: hello\ndescription: Minimal solo skill.\n---\n\n# hello\n' > plug/SKILL.md cat > plug/.claude-plugin/plugin.json <<'JSON' { "$schema": "https://json.schemastore.org/claude-code-plugin-manifest.json", "name": "hello", "version": "1.0.0" } JSON cd consumer && apm install --target claude ../plug ``` Actual: ``` [x] Failed to install APM dependencies: Local package is invalid: Failed to process Claude plugin: Unsupported schema-bearing plugin manifest: https://json.schemastore.org/claude-code-plugin-manifest.json. APM accepts schema-bearing plugin.json only with https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json; remove $schema only for a schema-less legacy plugin. ``` Expected: it installs as a legacy Claude plugin, which is what happens when `$schema` is absent. Also reproduces over the network against a real package: `apm install blader/humanizer`. `--force` does not bypass it. ## What varies | `plugin.json` location | `$schema` | Result | |---|---|---| | `.claude-plugin/` | Claude Code (schemastore) | `Unsupported schema-bearing plugin manifest` | | `.claude-plugin/` | agent-plugins.org | `must be admitted from the package root` | | `.claude-plugin/` | none | installs | | root `plugin.json` | Claude Code (schemastore) | `Unsupported schema-bearing plugin manifest`, raised earlier | Row 2 is the error the call site is actually reaching for. Row 1 is the same call raising before it can answer. Row 3 is what I expected row 1 to do. ## Root cause ```mermaid flowchart TD A["apm install
package with .claude-plugin/plugin.json"] --> B["detect_package_type
MARKETPLACE_PLUGIN"] B --> C["_validate_marketplace_plugin
validation.py:776"] C --> D["normalize_plugin_directory
plugin_parser.py:456
plugin.json = optional metadata"] D --> E{"classify_plugin_manifest_schema
local_bundle.py:79"} E -->|"no $schema"| F["return LEGACY
line 82"] E -->|"agent-plugins.org"| G["return AGENT_PLUGIN"] E -->|"any other $schema"| H["raise AgentPluginManifestError
line 94"] F --> I["plugin installs"] G --> J["raise AgentPluginLegacyBoundaryError
must be admitted from the package root"] H --> K["caught at validation.py:806
Failed to process Claude plugin"] K --> L["install fails"] style H fill:#ffe0e0 style L fill:#ffe0e0 ``` `classify_plugin_manifest_schema` is scoped to root manifests by its own definition. `local_bundle.py:72-73` reads: "Admission route selected exclusively by root plugin.json." It returns `LEGACY` when `$schema` is absent (line 82) and raises for any `$schema` it does not recognise (line 94). `normalize_plugin_directory` handles the legacy `.claude-plugin/` layout, where plugin.json is "treated as optional metadata" (`plugin_parser.py:460`). At line 489 it calls the router for one purpose only, to reject an Agent Plugins manifest placed outside the package root: ```python if classify_plugin_manifest_schema(manifest) is PluginSchemaRoute.AGENT_PLUGIN: raise AgentPluginLegacyBoundaryError( "Schema-bearing plugin.json must be admitted from the package root, " "not Claude plugin normalization" ) ``` With a Claude Code `$schema` the call raises, so the comparison never evaluates and the legacy path is unreachable. ## Suggested fix Treat an unrecognised `$schema` as `LEGACY` at this call site, either by catching `AgentPluginManifestError` around `plugin_parser.py:489` or by giving the router a non-raising variant for legacy admission. Strictness for a root `plugin.json` is unaffected. Happy to send a PR if you want the fix in that shape. Given the persona-review contract in CONTRIBUTING, I would rather confirm the approach with you first than guess at it. ## Why this shape appears in the wild `$schema` is a generic JSON Schema pointer, and Claude Code plugins normatively carry the schemastore URL. This project's own CHANGELOG entry for #1061 cites that schema when describing what `plugin.json` array entries must contain. Any marketplace shipping schema-conformant Claude plugins is affected, and the remedy in the error text asks authors to stop conforming to their own ecosystem's schema. ## Related * #2556: same package, different gate, fixed in 0.29.0. I verified that fix works: with `$schema` removed and `"skills": ["./"]` kept, `blader/humanizer` installs cleanly on 0.29.0. This report is the remaining barrier for that package. * #2654 introduced the schema admission. * #2735 and #2776 also concern package-type precedence, but they apply when a root `apm.yml` is present. This package has none. ## Environment apm 0.29.0 (`5ac6733`), macOS arm64. Line references are against v0.29.0.

issues.title: [BUG]  apm update  resets deployment target for virtual/claude_skill packages, ignoring  apm.yml 's  targets:  field
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
 apm update <packages>  incorrectly overwrites  deployments[].target  in  apm.lock.yaml  to  agents  for virtual/multi-file  claude_skill -type dependencies, even when  apm.yml  explicitly declares  targets: copilot  and no  --target  flag is passed on the command line. Running  apm install  afterward (same repo state, no flags) correctly re-derives the target from  apm.yml  and restores  copilot , so the update path and the install path disagree on target resolution for this package type.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. In a repo with  apm.yml  containing:
targets:
  - copilot
dependencies:
  apm:
    - angular/skills/angular-developer#main
    -  ...other deps
``` with `apm.lock.yaml` currently showing `deployments[].target: copilot` for all `angular-developer` deployed files (`.agents/skills/angular-developer/**`, `package_type: claude_skill`, `is_virtual: true`).
2. Run  apm update <owner/repo> [<owner/repo> ...] --yes  (listing dependencies including  angular/skills/angular-developer ), with or without  --target copilot .
3. Inspect  apm.lock.yaml .
4. See error: every  deployments[]  entry for  angular/skills/angular-developer  now has  target: agents  instead of  target: copilot . Reproduced identically across multiple consecutive runs in CI.

**Expected behavior**
 apm update  should resolve/preserve the deployment target the same way  apm install  does — from  apm.yml 's  targets:  field (or an explicit  --target  flag) — not from package-type heuristics. Running  apm install  immediately after confirms the correct target and touches nothing else, so the fix should just be aligning  apm update 's target resolution with  apm install 's.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

• OS: macOS (Darwin, arm64)
• Python Version: 3.14.7
• APM Version: 0.29.0
• VSCode Version (if relevant): N/A (ran via GitHub Actions CI / CLI)

**Logs**
No error output — the command exits successfully; the bug is silent lockfile corruption. Diff excerpt from an affected run:

- target: copilot
+ target: agents
  value: .agents/skills/angular-developer

(repeated for all 13 deployed files under  .agents/skills/angular-developer/ )

**Additional context**
Discovered via a scheduled CI workflow ( apm update  running against a lockfile with ~15 dependencies). Workaround in place: run  apm install  immediately after  apm update  in CI to re-sync targets before committing, which reliably restores the correct  copilot  target with no other changes to the lockfile.

issues.title: [BUG] Public release lookup fails when an ambient GitHub token is rejected
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
The Unix installer resolves `GITHUB_APM_PAT`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, or `GH_TOKEN` and attaches the selected credential to its first release-metadata request. When a credential is rejected, the response can lack `tag_name` and installation exits with `Invalid API response received`, even when the same public APM release metadata is accessible anonymously.

This makes bootstrap of a public CLI unnecessarily depend on an ambient credential's validity or authorization. Public CLI installation and authentication for subsequently consumed private packages are separate operations.

Public evidence:
- [Token selection and metadata request](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/13386d9937f92aa0105c59fc3c4b7bbff4a7c6d2/install.sh#L292-L338).
- [Retry conditions and error handling](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/13386d9937f92aa0105c59fc3c4b7bbff4a7c6d2/install.sh#L340-L396).
- #1582 and #1588 explain why credential-aware lookup was introduced: anonymous rate limits on shared IPs.

**To Reproduce**
1. Use an isolated installer harness with a non-secret dummy credential in one of the supported token environment variables.
2. Stub the canonical public release-metadata request to return an authentication rejection when Authorization is present, and valid release metadata when it is absent.
3. Run the installer with no pinned VERSION and observe that the current flow does not retry the rejected public metadata request anonymously before reporting failure. Stub subsequent downloads/install operations to keep the reproduction hermetic.

**Expected behavior**
- Fetch public APM release metadata without making a rejected ambient token a prerequisite for success.
- Preserve credential-aware recovery for anonymous rate limits; do not simply revert #1588 and reintroduce the shared-IP failure.
- Bound fallback to an explicitly public bootstrap context. Preserve private repository, GHES, enterprise mirror, and no-direct-fallback semantics; do not turn authorization failures into a general policy bypass.
- Keep credentials scoped to the intended host. Never send GitHub tokens to configured mirror hosts or log token values.
- Report HTTP/auth/rate-limit/network failures accurately, with an appropriate next action, rather than conflating them with malformed metadata or a private repository.
- Assess the corresponding release lookup used by `apm self-update` and platform installers so equivalent public-bootstrap paths remain consistent. Do not rewrite package authentication as part of this fix.
- Add regression cases for accepted/rejected/missing credentials, anonymous rate limits, pinned versions, private repositories, and fail-closed mirror behavior.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
- OS: macOS / Linux for the confirmed Unix installer path.
- Python Version: N/A for this shell metadata request.
- APM Version: v0.29.0 installer; same content at main revision `13386d9937f92aa0105c59fc3c4b7bbff4a7c6d2`.
- VSCode Version (if relevant): N/A.

**Logs**
N/A. The reproduction should use synthetic HTTP responses, not real credentials or organization-specific logs.

**Additional context**
Documenting a particular token lifetime or asking users to replace their primary credential is not the fix for downloading a public release. Private dependency access must continue to require the authorization appropriate to that dependency. #2788 is a separate proposal for credential diagnostics; it does not remove this bootstrap failure.

issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm cache prune` reports checkout entries as pruned even when deleting them fails.

The prune counter increments after calling `robust_rmtree(..., ignore_errors=True)`, which suppresses deletion errors.

**To Reproduce**

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Create an old checkout directory in the Git cache.
2. Make the checkout undeletable, for example by locking a file or denying removal permissions.
3. Run `apm cache prune --days 30`.
4. Observe that the command reports the checkout as pruned while the directory remains on disk.

A deterministic test case can mock `shutil.rmtree` to raise `PermissionError` and then call `GitCache.prune(max_age_days=30)`.

**Expected behavior**

Only successfully deleted checkout entries should be included in the pruned count.

If deletion fails, the entry should remain uncounted and the failure should be surfaced or reported as a warning.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

 - OS: Windows
 - Python Version: 3.14
 - APM Version: 0.29.1
 - VSCode Version (if relevant): Not relevant

Example incorrect output:

Pruned 1 checkout(s).

issues.title: [BUG] apm compile --target claude never resolves .context.md links when folding instructions into CLAUDE.md
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

`apm compile --target claude` folds instruction bodies (global + `applyTo`-scoped) directly
into `CLAUDE.md`, but never runs them through the markdown-link resolver. Any relative link
inside an instruction body — in particular a link to a `.apm/context/*.context.md` fragment —
is emitted byte-for-byte as written in the source file, with no adjustment for the fact that
`CLAUDE.md` may live in a different directory than the source instruction (e.g. when the
instruction comes from a dependency, or from a non-root placement).

The equivalent `AGENTS.md` pipeline (`agents_compiler.py` / `distributed_compiler.py`) does not
have this problem: it explicitly calls the link resolver
(`UnifiedLinkResolver.resolve_links_for_compilation` in `distributed_compiler.py`, or
`resolve_markdown_links` in `agents_compiler.py`) before returning the generated content.
`claude_formatter.py` has no equivalent call anywhere in the file — grepping the module for
`resolve_links` / `link_resolver` returns zero matches.

Practical effect: an instruction with no `applyTo` (global, e.g. a "signpost" file whose only
job is a short pointer to a `.context.md` file with the real content) will fold correctly into
`AGENTS.md` with a correctly rewritten link, but the *same* instruction, when it ends up folded
into `CLAUDE.md`, keeps the original unadjusted relative link and the link no longer resolves
from `CLAUDE.md`'s location.

**To Reproduce**

1. Create a package with one instruction and one context fragment it links to:

   ```
   my-pkg/
     apm.yml
     .apm/
       instructions/
         signpost.instructions.md
       context/
         conventions.context.md
   ```

   `apm.yml`:
   ```yaml
   name: my-pkg
   version: 0.0.1
   targets: [claude]
   dependencies:
     apm: []
   ```

   `.apm/instructions/signpost.instructions.md` (no `applyTo` — global instruction):
   ```markdown
   ---
   description: Signpost
   ---

   See [conventions](../context/conventions.context.md) for details.
   ```

   `.apm/context/conventions.context.md`:
   ```markdown
   Real content lives here.
   ```

2. Compile, forcing the instructions section into `CLAUDE.md` even though a
   `.claude/rules/` directory may already exist (`--force-instructions` is the fastest way to
   force the code path; the same missing resolution also affects the natural, non-forced path
   any time `.claude/rules/` is not yet populated, e.g. first `apm compile` run before
   `apm install`, or `apm compile --root <scratch>`):

   ```bash
   apm install --target claude
   apm compile --target claude --force-instructions
   ```

3. Inspect `CLAUDE.md`:

   ```markdown
   ## Project Standards

   ### Global Instructions

   See [conventions](../context/conventions.context.md) for details.
   ```

   The link `../context/conventions.context.md` is relative to
   `.apm/instructions/signpost.instructions.md`'s own directory (where it was authored), not to
   `CLAUDE.md`'s directory (project root). Resolved from `CLAUDE.md`'s location it points one
   directory above the project root and does not exist.

4. Compile the same package for `opencode` (or any other AGENTS.md-based target) instead:

   ```bash
   apm compile --target opencode
   ```

   `AGENTS.md` contains the *same* link, correctly rewritten to
   `.apm/context/conventions.context.md` (relative to the project root) — because
   `agents_compiler.py` / `distributed_compiler.py` do call the link resolver.

**Expected behavior**

`CLAUDE.md` should resolve the same relative links to `.context.md` / `.memory.md` fragments
that `AGENTS.md` already resolves correctly, using the same anchor (the compiled output file's
own directory), regardless of whether the instruction section is emitted via the normal path or
via `--force-instructions`.

**Environment:**
 - OS: Linux
 - Python Version: 3.13
 - APM Version: 0.30.0 (commit `8c2e0d9c`, tag `v0.30.0`)

**Logs**

No error is raised; the bug is a silently-wrong output (broken relative link), not a crash.

**Additional context**

Root cause, confirmed by reading the source at `v0.30.0`:

- `src/apm_cli/compilation/claude_formatter.py` builds the `CLAUDE.md` body in
  `_generate_claude_content()` and returns `"\n".join(sections)` directly — the file contains
  zero references to `resolve_links`, `resolve_markdown_links`, `link_resolver`, or
  `UnifiedLinkResolver` anywhere.
- Contrast with `src/apm_cli/compilation/distributed_compiler.py:754`, which — for the exact
  same kind of assembled `AGENTS.md` section content — explicitly calls:
  ```python
  content = self.link_resolver.resolve_links_for_compilation(
      content=content,
      source_file=placement.agents_path.parent,
      compiled_output=placement.agents_path,
  )
  ```
  right before returning, using a `UnifiedLinkResolver` instance that had `register_contexts()`
  called on it earlier in the same compile pass.
- `src/apm_cli/compilation/agents_compiler.py` additionally calls the (simpler,
  content-inlining) `resolve_markdown_links()` helper from `link_resolver.py` in its own
  non-distributed rendering path (`generate_output()`, lines ~1467 and ~1658).
- `claude_formatter.py` has no equivalent of either call.

I verified the fix locally by adding the missing call, mirroring the `distributed_compiler.py`
pattern:

1. In `ClaudeFormatter.__init__`, construct a resolver once: `self.link_resolver =
   UnifiedLinkResolver(self.source_dir)`.
2. In `ClaudeFormatter.format_distributed`, before generating any placement content, call
   `self.link_resolver.register_contexts(primitives)`.
3. In `ClaudeFormatter._generate_claude_content`, right before `return`, replace
   `return "\n".join(sections)` with:
   ```python
   content = "\n".join(sections)
   content = self.link_resolver.resolve_links_for_compilation(
       content=content,
       source_file=placement.claude_path.parent,
       compiled_output=placement.claude_path,
   )
   return content
   ```

With this change, the reproduction above produces the correctly-resolved
`.apm/context/conventions.context.md` link in `CLAUDE.md`, identical to what `AGENTS.md`
already produces for the same source instruction. I'm happy to open a PR with this patch (plus
a regression test) if that's useful — flagging as an issue first in case there's a preferred
approach or a reason this was intentionally left out that I'm not aware of.

Separately (not part of this report, noting for completeness): I checked whether other
per-target root-context formatters have the same gap. `gemini_formatter.py` also has no
`resolve_links` call, but it turns out to be a 12-line stub that only ever emits a single
`@./AGENTS.md` import line and never assembles instruction content itself, so it isn't affected.
No other target has its own root-context formatter (`cursor` doesn't produce one; `copilot`,
`codex`, `opencode`, `windsurf`, `antigravity` all share the correctly-resolving `AGENTS.md`
pipeline).

issues.title: Install fails on Windows with WinError 206 (path too long) / WinError 3 due to double-hashed staging paths
issues.body:
Install fails on Windows with WinError 206 (path too long) / WinError 3 due to double-hashed staging paths

**Environment:**
- OS: Windows 11 Pro (10.0.26100)
- Shell: PowerShell
- Command: `apm install <my-package-source> --target claude`
- Project root: `C:\<my-path-30-chars>`

**Description:**

Installing the `<my-packages>` dependency fails on Windows because the resolver stages replacement files under a path that exceeds the Windows `MAX_PATH` (260 character) limit. Every failing file follows the same pattern — a `.apm-resolution-staging\<32-char hash>\replacements\<64-char hash>\...` structure appended on top of the already-long checkout path and the package's own nested folder names (e.g. `backlog\release-notes\.apm\skills\aitoolkit-backlog-release-notes-skill`).

**Command run:**
```
apm install <my-package-source> --target claude
```

**Observed output (excerpt):**
```
[x] 1 package failed:
  +- <my-package-source> -- Failed to download dependency <my-package-dependency>:
[('...checkouts_v1\...\sparse-...\profiles\shared\packages\backlog\release-notes\.apm\prompts\aitoolkit-backlog-release-notes.prompt.md',
'...apm_modules\.apm-resolution-staging\5eeb88cb...\replacements\93d0a232...\backlog\release-notes\.apm\prompts\aitoolkit-backlog-release-notes.prompt.md',
'[WinError 3] The system cannot find the path specified'),
...
'[WinError 206] The filename or extension is too long: ...\backlog\release-notes\.apm\skills\aitoolkit-backlog-release-notes-skill'"),
...
```

**Root cause (my analysis):**

The destination path built by the resolver is something like:
```
C:\<my-path-30-chars>\apm_modules\.apm-resolution-staging\5eeb88cb5cf84db5b6df5fccc2f33cfc\replacements\93d0a232a5d070466326b08efbb0bd5ebc195148afa09606a8e8e727999fb6fc\backlog\release-notes\.apm\skills\aitoolkit-backlog-release-notes-skill
```
This is well over 260 characters. On Windows, without long-path support explicitly enabled and used by every layer in the chain (OS, git, and the Python runtime `apm` is built on), file/directory operations at this depth fail with `WinError 206` (path too long) or the related `WinError 3` (parent directory silently failed to be created, so it "can't find" it later).

This reproduces consistently for every package in this dependency that has moderately deep nested folder names (`sprint-planning`, `sprint-review`, `status-report`, `release-notes`), since the two long hex-hash segments (`.apm-resolution-staging\<hash>\replacements\<hash>\`) added by the resolver push otherwise-reasonable paths over the Windows limit.

**Expected behavior:**

The install should succeed on Windows, or `apm` should proactively detect/avoid excessively long staging paths (e.g., by using shorter hash prefixes, flattening the staging structure, or opting into Windows extended-length path syntax `\\?\` internally).

**Suggested fix:**
Shorten the staging directory naming scheme (e.g., truncate hashes, or avoid nesting `.apm-resolution-staging\<hash>\replacements\<hash>\` under the project's own `apm_modules` path).

**Workarounds attempted:**
- Enabling `LongPathsEnabled` in the registry and `git config --global core.longpaths true` (not authorized by company policy)
- Moving the project to a shorter root path (huge impact on other projects).

Thank you.

### Findings

#### [F] Sequential registry lookups where parallel lookups already exist as a pattern -- src/apm_cli/registry/operations.py:292-310

- Current: O(n) sequential network round-trips. `batch_fetch_server_info()` loops over `server_references` and calls `self.registry_client.find_server_by_reference(server_ref)` once per server, in series, despite each call being an independent HTTP request (registry search + get_server, see `src/apm_cli/registry/client.py:704-737`).

- Fix: Wrap the loop body of `batch_fetch_server_info` in a bounded `ThreadPoolExecutor` (reuse the `max_workers=4` convention from `check_servers_needing_installation`) so per-server registry lookups run concurrently instead of sequentially.
- Impact: `batch_fetch_server_info` is called from `collect_runtime_variables` (line 333) and `collect_environment_variables` (line 411) in the same file, both invoked during MCP install flows with potentially many server references -- each currently pays full sequential network latency.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Interactive selection of installed plugins for removal
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Managing plugins currently requires browsing a static table, copying or typing a package identifier, and running a separate command. Removal is particularly awkward when installed identities include a host, repository, and package subpath. Users should be able to select installed plugins by their recognizable names without reconstructing those identifiers.

#2749 already proposes interactive package selection for installation/search. This request covers the complementary removal workflow so adding and removing plugins can share a consistent interaction.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Provide an opt-in interactive removal picker, for example `apm uninstall --interactive` and `apm uninstall --interactive --global` (exact command shape subject to maintainer preference).

- List installed plugins in the selected project or user scope, showing their name, source, and scope.
- Support filtering and selecting one or more plugins.
- Resolve selections directly to their installed dependency identities, including marketplace packages, rather than asking users to type aliases or full paths.
- Show the removal plan and ask for confirmation before applying it through the existing uninstall implementation. Cancellation must leave the installation unchanged.
- Keep scripted/non-interactive commands available; do not hang waiting for input in CI or without a suitable terminal.

Align the picker with the installation UX proposed in #2749. Reuse existing dependency ownership and removal rules rather than adding a separate cleanup mechanism.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

Use `apm deps list`, then copy the installed dependency into `apm uninstall`. This works as a command-line workflow, but long identifiers and truncated terminal tables make it inconvenient. A shell wrapper with an external picker would duplicate scope and identity handling outside APM.

**Additional context**

Requested after exercising marketplace registration, global installation, updates, and removal with APM 0.30.0. The goal is a small, consistent interactive workflow for adding and removing plugins, not a full-screen package-management application.

Related installation proposal: #2749.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Per-primitive `targets:` frontmatter for file primitives (instructions, prompts, skills, agents)
issues.body:
## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

Teams increasingly share one repository across several coding agents at once (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Cursor, Copilot). APM supports this at **package** granularity: a dependency entry's `targets:` list (#1911) routes a whole package. But the packages such teams want to share are multi-target *by design* — most of their primitives are portable and one or two are harness-specific. There is currently no way to express that.

Concrete case. A team wants a `simplify` instruction because OpenCode has no equivalent default. Claude Code already provides equivalent behavior, so shipping the same instruction there is redundant and potentially conflicting context. The intended result:

```
.apm/
└── instructions/
    ├── coding-standards.instructions.md   → all targets
    ├── security.instructions.md           → all targets
    └── simplify.instructions.md           → opencode only
```

Today the only options are:

1. **Ship it everywhere.** Every harness gets the primitive. Redundant where the harness already does this, and a second source of truth for behavior the harness owns.
2. **Fork the package** per target. This is the duplication-and-drift problem per-package routing exists to prevent — a fix to the shared `security` instruction now has to be applied in N packages.

Note the gap is specifically *deliverable but unwanted*. The compatibility matrix already handles "cannot be delivered" (e.g. `hooks / opencode = unsupported` is skipped silently), and the `unsupported` cells are not a substitute for what is asked here: every cell involved in this request is `native` or `compiled`. The matrix answers "can this reach harness Y", not "should it".

## Describe the solution you'd like

Declare `targets:` in file-primitive frontmatter:

```yaml
---
description: Simplify implementation and reduce unnecessary complexity.
targets:
  - opencode
---
```

**Semantics**

- Effective targets = primitive `targets:` ∩ the invocation's install targets. A primitive can never widen reach onto a target the invocation excluded.
- **No `targets:` key → existing behavior, unchanged.** Backward compatible; no existing package needs edits.
- List form only, matching the existing `apm.yml` preference for plural `targets:` as a YAML list. `targets: ["*"]` optional, as explicit-universal sugar.
- Slugs are target-catalog slugs (`opencode`, `claude`, …), never output directories (`.opencode/`). Source configuration stays independent of how a target renders.
- **Unknown slug fails closed** — the primitive routes nowhere, with a diagnostic naming the offending token and listing supported targets. A typo like `open code` that silently routes nowhere is a worse failure than a hard error.
- Filtering happens **before target-specific rendering**, so a skipped primitive produces no target artifact and does not consume a name/slot in the target's namespace.
- Applies to file-based primitives: instructions, prompts, skills, agents — and hooks if/when per-file hook targeting lands. MCP is tracked separately in #2606.

**Expected processing**

```
discover primitive
  └─ read frontmatter
       ├─ no `targets:` ──────────────► existing behavior
       └─ `targets:` present
            ├─ current target ∈ targets ─► render ─► deploy
            └─ otherwise ────────────────► skip (no artifact)
```

**Composition with package-level targeting**

Package-level and primitive-level targeting are complementary, not competing:

```
apm install --target opencode
  Primitive A  targets: [opencode]  → included
  Primitive B  targets: [claude]    → excluded
  Primitive C  no targets           → included (existing behavior)

apm install --target claude
  Primitive A  targets: [opencode]  → excluded
  Primitive B  targets: [claude]    → included
  Primitive C  no targets           → included (existing behavior)
```

## How this relates to #1911 ruling 2

Ruling 2 declines per-primitive-**type** routing for inert primitives (#1898): "splitting one package's skills to one harness and its instructions to another is a *fork* of that package." That reasoning is sound and this request does not reopen it — the unit here is still one package routed to whichever harnesses receive it, and this request is confined to one primitive type.

What is asked for is file granularity *within* a type, and the project has already accepted that granularity is needed wherever the deprecated filename convention was the only way to reach it:

- **#2261** requests per-file target declaration for hooks, and observes that the #2031 deprecation of filename-based routing "has no successor."
- **#2606** requests the same scoping for `dependencies.mcp` entries.
- This issue is the remaining instance of that same gap: the primitives with no filename convention to lean on and no proposal covering them — `.instructions.md`, `.prompt.md`, `SKILL.md`, `.agent.md`.

If maintainers prefer the #2261 shape (glob rules in `apm.yml`) extended to these primitive types rather than frontmatter, that resolves the same problem and I'd be glad to see it — see alternatives 3/5 below. The mechanism is the maintainers' call; the granularity is the ask.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

1. **Fork the package per target.** Rejected: it is the duplication and synchronization burden that per-package routing was introduced to eliminate, and it puts the shared `security` instruction in N places.
2. **A filename convention** (`simplify.opencode.instructions.md`). Rejected: #2031 is retiring exactly this class of implicit convention after #2020 showed it silently mis-routing. Adding a second one recreates the surface being removed.
3. **Extend #2261's glob-rule model to all file primitives** (`apm.yml` → `primitives.instructions: [{files: "...", targets: [...]}]`). Viable — it keeps all routing in one place and inherits the last-match-wins semantics. Trade-off: routing drifts from the primitive it governs (an author editing `.apm/instructions/x.md` must remember to check `apm.yml`), and a consumed `.apm/` subtree loses its own routing metadata. Co-located frontmatter keeps the declaration with the thing declared, which is why it is proposed here.
4. **Rely on the compatibility matrix.** Rejected: `unsupported` cells express capability, not author intent, and every primitive involved here is already supported on every target concerned.
5. **An `apm.yml` block keyed by primitive path.** Equivalent to 3 with a different spelling; same drift trade-off.

## Acceptance criteria

1. File-based primitives (instructions, prompts, skills, agents) accept a `targets:` frontmatter list.
2. Given `targets: [opencode]`, the primitive is rendered and deployed for OpenCode and for no other target.
3. Given `targets: [opencode, claude]`, it deploys to both.
4. A primitive with no `targets:` key behaves exactly as today.
5. Primitive-level targeting composes with `apm.yml` `targets:` and `--target` by intersection — never by union; a primitive cannot reach a target the invocation excluded.
6. No unwanted artifacts: a skipped primitive produces no target output (an OpenCode-only instruction creates nothing under `.claude/`) and is not reported as drift by `apm audit`.
7. An unknown target slug fails closed with a diagnostic that lists the supported targets.
8. `apm audit` and a dry run surface the filtering decision per primitive (e.g. `Would skip: simplify.instructions.md (targets: [opencode])`).
9. Documented in author-primitives, `concepts/primitives-and-targets`, and `reference/targets-matrix`.
10. Backward compatible: existing packages install unchanged.

## Additional context

**Related issues**

- #1911 — [DESIGN] per-package primitive routing, the north star this composes with.
- #2261 — per-file target declaration for hooks; same gap, different primitive.
- #2606 — per-dependency `targets:` scoping for `dependencies.mcp`; same gap, MCP.
- #2031 — retiring filename-based hook routing; the precedent for not adding implicit conventions.
- #1882 — making missing targets a hard error; relevant to criterion 7's fail-closed posture.

**Repository-shape example**

```
project/
├── apm.yml
└── .apm/
    ├── instructions/
    │   ├── coding-standards.instructions.md   # no targets → all
    │   ├── security.instructions.md           # no targets → all
    │   └── simplify.instructions.md           # targets: [opencode]
    ├── skills/
    └── prompts/
```

**Resulting deployment**

```
             ┌──────────────┬──────────────┬──────────────┐
             ▼              ▼              ▼
          OpenCode      Claude Code       Codex
             │              │              │
     coding-standards  coding-standards  coding-standards
     security          security          security
     simplify          --                --
```

The package remains shared and single-sourced; each primitive declares its own reach.

I'm happy to help with design, implementation, or testing on this if it's in scope — and equally happy to be pointed at the existing mechanism if one already covers it.

issues.title: [cli-consistency] CLI Consistency Report - 2026-09-15
issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-09-15
**APM Version**: Agent Package Manager (APM) CLI version 0.30.0 (6f3dd39)
**Commands Inspected**: 23 (`--help` for top-level, init, install, uninstall, update, compile, run, deps + 5 subcommands, mcp + 3 subcommands, config + 3 subcommands, runtime + 1 subcommand)

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 0 |
| Medium | 1 |
| Low | 2 |

---

### Medium Severity

#### Confusing "bug in command routing" message for a plain user typo
- **Command**: `apm config get <invalid-key>` / `apm config set <invalid-key> <value>`
- **Problem**: When a user passes an unrecognized configuration key (a simple typo, e.g. `apm config get badkeyxyz`), APM prints a generic "Unknown configuration key" message followed by: `"This error may indicate a bug in command routing. Please report this issue."` This wording tells the user their own typo might be an APM bug and invites them to file a spurious issue report, when in fact this is ordinary invalid-input handling (same category as Click's own "No such option" / "Invalid value" messages elsewhere in the CLI, which are phrased neutrally).
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm config get badkeyxyz
  [x] Unknown configuration key: 'badkeyxyz'
  [i] Valid keys: auto-integrate, target, self-update.channel,
  self-update.install-dir, mcp-registry-url, temp-dir, allow-protocol-fallback,
  prefer-ssh
  [i] This error may indicate a bug in command routing. Please report this issue.
  ```
  Source: `src/apm_cli/commands/config.py` lines ~540 and ~697 (`_valid_config_keys()` callers in both the `set` and `get` code paths).
- **Suggested Fix**: Drop the "bug in command routing" sentence for this user-input-validation path (or reserve it for a genuinely unreachable internal-consistency case), and instead end with a plain hint such as `Run 'apm config list' to see all settable keys.` This keeps the tone consistent with other invalid-argument errors in the CLI (e.g. `apm runtime setup badruntime` -> `Error: Invalid value for ...`, no "report this issue" language).

---

### Low Severity

#### Inconsistent trailing-period style across option/command help strings
- **Command**: All commands (`apm --help`, `apm install --help`, `apm compile --help`, etc.)
- **Problem**: Built-in `--help`/`--version` descriptions and a handful of option descriptions end with a trailing period (e.g. `"Show this message and exit."`, `"(deprecated) Use 'apm plugin init' instead."`), while the large majority of command and flag descriptions across the same `--help` screens do not end with a period (e.g. `"Manage APM package dependencies"`, `"List installed APM dependencies and their primitives"`). Neither convention is wrong on its own, but the mixing is visible within the same screen (compare `apm --help`'s command list, none of which end in a period except `config` and `self-update`, against option blocks where roughly 30 of ~77 sampled option lines end with a period and the rest do not).
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  Commands:
    approve       Approve executable primitives (hooks, MCP, LSP, bin,...
    config        Configure APM CLI.
    deny          Deny executable primitives for packages (a narrowing...
    self-update   Update the APM CLI binary itself to the latest version.
    targets       Show resolved targets for the current project.
  ```
  Here `config`, `self-update`, `targets`, `unpack`, `publish`, `pack`, and `lifecycle` end in a period while most sibling entries (`approve`, `audit`, `deny`, `deps`, `doctor`, `find`, `install`, `uninstall`) do not.
- **Suggested Fix**: Standardize on one style for the one-line command/flag summaries shown in `--help` output (recommend: no trailing period, matching the majority convention already used for most commands and options), and apply it consistently across `cli.py` and subcommand modules.

#### Error output mixes Click's `Error:` prefix with the custom `[x]` bracket convention
- **Command**: `apm install --target badtarget`, `apm compile --target badtarget`
- **Problem**: The project's own encoding/status-symbol convention (documented in the repo's ASCII style rules) uses `[x]` for errors, `[i]` for info, etc. However, for invalid `--target` values, Click's own `Error:` prefix and the custom `[x]` marker both appear on the same line, producing a slightly redundant/mixed presentation compared to plain Click errors elsewhere (e.g. `apm deps info` with no argument only shows Click's `Error: Missing argument 'PACKAGE'.`, no `[x]`).
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  $ apm install --target badtarget
  Usage: apm install [OPTIONS] [PACKAGES]...
  Try 'apm install --help' for help.

  Error: [x] Unknown target 'badtarget'

  Valid targets: agent-skills, agents, agy, all, antigravity, claude, codex, copilot, ...
  ```
  vs.
  ```
  $ apm deps info
  Usage: apm deps info [OPTIONS] PACKAGE
  Try 'apm deps info --help' for help.

  Error: Missing argument 'PACKAGE'.
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Pick one convention for CLI-argument validation errors raised via Click's `UsageError`/`BadParameter` path: either always prefix with the custom `[x]` marker (and suppress Click's own `Error:` label), or never include `[x]` when Click already renders `Error:`. Consistency here mostly affects readability, not correctness.

---

### Clean Areas

- **Installation & versioning**: `apm --version` and `apm --help` work correctly and match the documented version format.
- **Help text availability**: `--help` works on every top-level command and every subcommand tested (`init`, `install`, `uninstall`, `update`, `compile`, `run`, `deps` + `list`/`tree`/`info`/`clean`/`update`, `mcp` + `search`/`show`/`install`, `config` + `set`/`get`/`list`, `runtime` + `setup`) with no crashes or missing help text.
- **Flag naming consistency**: Common flags (`-v/--verbose`, `-g/--global`, `-y/--yes`, `--dry-run`, `--force`, `--parallel-downloads`, `--legacy-skill-paths`) use identical spelling and short-flag letters across every command that supports them; no `--dryrun` or similar naming drift was found.
- **Exit behavior**: All tested invalid-argument scenarios (`apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` with no argument, `apm config set` with no argument, `apm mcp show` with no argument, `apm runtime setup badruntime`, `apm nonexistentcommand`) produced clean, actionable error messages with exit code 2 (or 1 for MCP registry lookups) -- no stack traces or tracebacks were observed anywhere.
- **Documentation cross-reference**: All commands and subcommands checked against `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/*.md` (`config.md`, `deps.md`, `install.md`, `mcp.md`, `runtime.md`) match the live CLI: documented flags (`--target`/`-t`, `--limit`, `--registry`, target value lists including experimental `openclaw`/`agy`/`copilot-app`/`copilot-cowork`/`grok-cloud`) and documented default values (`apm mcp search --limit 10`, `apm mcp list --limit 20`, `apm install --parallel-downloads 4`) all matched actual `--help` output and runtime behavior exactly. `README.md`'s `apm lock export --format cyclonedx|spdx` reference was also verified against `apm lock export --help`.
- **Runtime subcommands**: `apm runtime status` and `apm runtime list` output matched the documented preference order (`copilot -> codex -> gemini -> llm`) and supported-runtime table exactly.

Note: The task referenced `docs/cli-reference.md`, which does not exist as a single file in this repository; the equivalent, more granular documentation lives under `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/*.md` (one file per command) and was used for cross-referencing instead.

issues.title: [perf-scan] 2026-09-16 -- performance opportunities found
issues.body:
## Performance Scan - 2026-09-16

Automated scan of src/apm_cli/ for algorithmic performance anti-patterns.
1 finding identified.

### Findings

#### [E] Heavy top-level imports on CLI Startup -- src/apm_cli/cli.py:20-57

- Current: `apm_cli/cli.py` unconditionally imports all 25+ command modules
  at module level (`from apm_cli.commands.install import install`,
  `from apm_cli.commands.audit import audit`, `from apm_cli.commands.pack
  import pack_cmd, unpack_cmd`, etc.). `commands/install.py` alone pulls in
  53 top-level imports spanning `install/pipeline.py`, `install/services.py`,
  `install/validation.py` (which imports `requests`), MCP integration,
  security scanning, and GitLab/Artifactory resolvers. Every one of these
  transitive chains is imported on every CLI invocation, including
  `apm --help`, `apm doctor`, or `apm config get`, regardless of which
  subcommand the user actually runs.
- Proposed: Defer heavyweight subcommand modules (`install`, `audit`,
  `pack`, `marketplace`, `uninstall`, `update`) to a lazy-loading Click
  group (`click.Group` subclass overriding `get_command`/`list_commands`
  to `importlib.import_module` on demand) so only the invoked subcommand's
  transitive import graph loads.
- Fix: Convert `apm_cli/cli.py`'s top-level command imports into a lazy
  dispatch table keyed by command name, importing each command module's
  `commands.<name>` submodule only inside `get_command()` when that name
  is actually requested, cutting cold-start import cost for `--help` and
  low-weight commands (`doctor`, `config`, `targets`).

### Scan coverage

- src/apm_cli/ (484 files scanned)
- Patterns checked: A (quadratic loops), B (linear scan in loop),
  C (unconditional expensive ops), D (redundant config parsing),
  E (heavy top-level imports), F (sequential independent I/O)

Patterns A-D and F were reviewed across the highest-candidate files
(commands/uninstall/engine.py, integration/hook_integrator.py,
deps/plugin_parser.py, core/script_runner.py, compilation/context_optimizer.py,
registry/operations.py, install/plan.py, install/target_filter.py,
commands/deps/cli.py) and found to already use appropriate data
structures (set/dict-keyed dedup, precomputed indexes, bounded loops
over small collections such as install targets or hook events) or
existing caching (`_pattern_cache`, `_directory_cache`,
`ThreadPoolExecutor` in `registry/operations.py`). No additional
confirmed findings for those patterns.

issues.title: [FEATURE] Fall back to native Git credential helper for Azure DevOps authentication
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

Azure DevOps Services dependencies currently require either `ADO_APM_PAT` or an active Azure CLI session (`az login`). When neither is available, APM does not fall back to the native Git credential helper, even when the same repository can be accessed successfully with Git itself:

```bash
git clone https://dev.azure.com/org/project/_git/repo
```

This is inconvenient for users who already authenticate to Azure DevOps through Git Credential Manager or another configured Git credential helper. It also makes ADO behave differently from other supported Git hosts where APM can delegate authentication to Git.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

When installing a package from Azure DevOps Services (`dev.azure.com` or a supported `*.visualstudio.com` URL), APM should use the native Git credential helper as a fallback when:

1. `ADO_APM_PAT` is not set; and
2. Azure CLI authentication is unavailable, not installed, or the user is not signed in.

The fallback should invoke Git using the user's existing credential-helper configuration, without requiring APM-specific environment variables or embedding credentials in repository URLs. The behavior should be equivalent to a direct `git clone` or `git ls-remote` against the same repository.

The intended authentication order would be:

1. `ADO_APM_PAT`;
2. Azure CLI bearer authentication from `az login`;
3. native Git credential helper;
4. an actionable authentication error if all methods fail.

The implementation should remain non-interactive in APM's subprocesses, preserve current credential redaction and isolation guarantees, and avoid changing Azure DevOps Server's existing PAT-only behavior unless explicitly intended. Tests should cover helper-based HTTPS authentication, unavailable `az`, PAT and bearer precedence, and failure diagnostics.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**

- Continue requiring `ADO_APM_PAT`, which duplicates credentials that users may already have stored in Git Credential Manager.
- Require users to run `az login`, which is not always available in minimal environments, containers, or setups where Git Credential Manager is the established authentication path.
- Use SSH URLs and SSH keys instead of HTTPS, which changes the dependency URL and is not always available for Azure DevOps users.

**Additional context**

Related authentication behavior is documented in [Azure DevOps authentication](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/main/docs/src/content/docs/getting-started/authentication.md#azure-devops).

I would be happy to help with reproduction, design feedback, or testing.

## Performance Scan - 2026-09-18

Automated scan of src/apm_cli/ for algorithmic performance anti-patterns.
No confirmed findings.

### Scan coverage

- src/apm_cli/ (484 files scanned)
- Patterns checked: A (quadratic loops), B (linear scan in loop),
  C (unconditional expensive ops), D (redundant config parsing),
  E (heavy top-level imports), F (sequential independent I/O)

### Notes

Candidate matches were reviewed across all six patterns and discarded as
false positives:

- Pattern A: high for-loop-count files (uninstall/engine.py,

  per-directory collections (candidate placements, hook events, plugin

  exact_index/plugin_index in _resolve_marketplace_packages, pool dict

  avoid O(n^2) scans.
- Pattern B: `if x in dict`/`set` membership checks found throughout
  install/, deps/, and commands/ are already against pre-built
  sets/dicts (seen_keys, locked_keys, allowed_hosts, exact_index), not
  raw lists.
- Pattern C: os.walk/glob calls (deployable_source_plan.py,
  plugin_parser.py, policy/discovery.py) run once per package/scan
  invocation, not in a per-item hot loop.
- Pattern D: script_runner.py's `_load_config()` and registry/
  operations.py's repeated `os.getenv()` calls are called at most a
  handful of times per command invocation, not in a per-dependency loop.
- Pattern E: CLI command modules (install.py, audit.py, etc.) already

  stdlib/click imports remain at module level.
- Pattern F: subprocess.run calls inside loops (bare_cache.py,
  github_downloader.py) are sequential git config/fetch/checkout steps
  with a data dependency (fetch must precede checkout), not
  independent per-package I/O; parallel download phases already use
  ThreadPoolExecutor (install/phases/download.py, deps/apm_resolver.py,
  deps/revision_pins.py, registry/operations.py).

issues.title: [BUG] prune marks a declared GitHub package orphaned after a casing-only manifest change
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

In APM 0.31.0, changing only the GitHub owner/repository casing in a dependency declaration causes `apm prune --dry-run` to classify the installed package as orphaned.

**To Reproduce**

1. With APM 0.31.0, create this manifest and run `apm install`:

   ```yaml
   name: prune-fixture
   version: 1.0.0
   targets:
     - agent-skills
   dependencies:
     apm:
       - microsoft/apm#v0.31.0
     mcp: []
   ```

2. Confirm that the package is materialized at `apm_modules/microsoft/apm`.

3. Change only `microsoft/apm` to `Microsoft/APM` in the dependency declaration:

   ```yaml
   dependencies:
     apm:
       - Microsoft/APM#v0.31.0
   ```

4. Run `apm prune --dry-run` without reinstalling:

   ```text
   [>] Analyzing installed packages vs apm.yml...
   [!] Found 1 orphaned package(s):
   [!]   - microsoft/apm (would be removed)
   [*] Dry run complete - no changes made
   ```

**Expected behavior**

The existing package is recognized as the declared GitHub dependency. Changing GitHub owner/repository casing does not change package identity or make the package orphaned.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

- OS: macOS
- Python Version: 3.14.7
- APM Version: 0.31.0 (Homebrew); also reproduced with current `main`
- VSCode Version (if relevant): Not applicable

**Logs**

The complete relevant output is included in the reproduction above.

**Additional context**

GitHub package identity is [normalized to lowercase](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/98616b9430140275a3a7c8fefb25d8d111cecc4e/src/apm_cli/models/dependency/identity.py#L65-L90), while materialization paths [preserve source casing](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/98616b9430140275a3a7c8fefb25d8d111cecc4e/src/apm_cli/models/dependency/materialization.py#L106-L110). Prune [compares expected and scanned materialization paths directly](https://github.com/microsoft/apm/blob/98616b9430140275a3a7c8fefb25d8d111cecc4e/src/apm_cli/commands/prune.py#L125-L149).

This is distinct from #3015: that report concerns a genuine orphan not being detected; this report concerns a declared package being falsely detected as orphaned.

issues.title: [BUG]: UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte on Windows during 'apm install'
issues.body:
Description
On Windows environments (PowerShell / Command Prompt), running apm install fails with a UnicodeDecodeError in the underlying subprocess reader thread when resolving dependencies. This happens because Python defaults to the system code page (gbk / CP936 on Simplified Chinese Windows) rather than UTF-8 when reading standard output/error from spawned child processes (e.g., git or sub-commands with UTF-8 characters).

Steps to Reproduce
Run PowerShell on a Windows system using standard Chinese locale (chcp 936).

Add dependencies containing UTF-8 characters (e.g., non-ASCII commit logs, quotes, or descriptions) in apm.yml.

Run:

PowerShell
apm install ; apm compile
Observe the exception during package resolution.

Expected Behavior
apm should handle process I/O using UTF-8 explicitly (e.g., setting encoding="utf-8", errors="replace" or errors="backslashreplace" in subprocess.Popen / stream readers), allowing dependency resolution to finish without crashing regardless of the OS system locale.

Actual Behavior / Stack Trace
Plaintext
PS D:\2-gerrit\Jenkins\jenkins-platform.worktrees\workflow> apm install ; apm compile
[>] Installing dependencies from apm.yml...
[>] Resolving lsp-infra-hub-jenkins-cli...
[>] Resolving awesome-copilot-multi-stage-dockerfile...
[>] Resolving lsp-infra-hub-apm-skill-creator...
Exception in thread Thread-64 (_readerthread):
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "threading.py", line 1075, in _bootstrap_inner
  File "threading.py", line 1012, in run
  File "subprocess.py", line 1599, in _readerthread
UnicodeDecodeError: 'gbk' codec can't decode byte 0x94 in position 711: illegal multibyte sequence
Environment
OS: Windows (Simplified Chinese, default codepage 936 / GBK)

Shell: PowerShell

Tool: APM (Agent Package Manager)

Python Version: 3.x

issues.body:
## CLI Consistency Report

**Date**: 2026-09-24
**APM Version**: Agent Package Manager (APM) CLI version 0.31.0 (0bd8da6)
**Commands Inspected**: 31 top-level commands (`apm --help`) plus 22 explicitly-requested command/subcommand `--help` invocations (init, install, uninstall, update, compile, run, deps [+list/tree/info/clean/update], mcp [+search/show/install], config [+set/get/list], runtime [+setup]), plus spot checks on `search`, `find`, `marketplace`, `lock` for cross-reference and error-handling validation.

### Summary

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| High | 0 |
| Medium | 1 |
| Low | 1 |

No high-severity issues were found: every command reachable from `apm --help` and every documented command under `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/` exists on both sides, `--help` works on every command/subcommand tested, invalid input produces clean `Usage:`/`Error:` messages with exit code 2 (no stack traces), and flag documentation for `install`, `deps`, `mcp`, `config`, `runtime`, and `init` in the docs matches the live CLI output closely, including target-value lists and default values.

---

### Medium Severity

#### Inconsistent trailing-period punctuation in command summaries

- **Command**: `apm --help`, `apm deps --help`, `apm mcp --help`
- **Problem**: Top-level and subcommand one-line summaries mix trailing periods and no periods with no discernible rule (not simply "truncated vs not truncated" -- several complete, non-truncated summaries end with a period while other complete summaries do not).
- **Evidence** (from `apm --help`):
  ```
  config        Configure APM CLI.
  lifecycle     Inspect, test, and scaffold lifecycle scripts.
  pack          Pack distributable artifacts from your APM project.
  publish       Publish a package to a registry.
  self-update   Update the APM CLI binary itself to the latest version.
  targets       Show resolved targets for the current project.
  unpack        [Deprecated] Extract an APM bundle into the current project.
  ---
  cache         Manage the local package cache
  compile       Compile APM context into distributed AGENTS.md files
  deps          Manage APM package dependencies
  init          Initialize a new APM project
  list          List available scripts in the current project
  ```
  Same pattern recurs one level down, e.g. `apm mcp --help`:
  ```
  install  Add an MCP server to apm.yml.
  list     List all available MCP servers
  search   Search MCP servers in registry
  show     Show detailed MCP server information
  ```
  and `apm deps --help`:
  ```
  clean   Remove all APM dependencies
  update  DEPRECATED: use 'apm update' instead (strict superset).
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Pick one convention (Click/argparse community norm is "no trailing period" for one-line summaries) and apply it uniformly across all `@click.command(help=...)` / docstring-derived summaries in `src/apm_cli/cli.py` and subcommand modules.

---

### Low Severity

#### Deprecation notices use four different textual conventions

- **Command**: `apm --help`, `apm deps update --help`, `apm init --help`
- **Problem**: Deprecated commands/flags are flagged with inconsistent markers: `[Deprecated]`, `DEPRECATED:`, `Deprecated:`, and `(deprecated)`.
- **Evidence**:
  ```
  unpack        [Deprecated] Extract an APM bundle into the current project.
  update  DEPRECATED: use 'apm update' instead (strict superset).
  --target             ... Deprecated: run 'apm update --target' instead.   (apm deps update --help)
  --plugin                   (deprecated) Use 'apm plugin init' instead.    (apm init --help)
  --marketplace              (deprecated) Use 'apm marketplace init' instead. (apm init --help)
  ```
- **Suggested Fix**: Standardize on a single marker/casing (e.g. always `[Deprecated]` at the start of the summary) across command list entries and flag help text so users can grep/scan consistently.

---

### Clean Areas

- **Installation & versioning**: `apm --version` and `apm --help` work as documented; no install issues.
- **Command/doc parity**: every command in `docs/src/content/docs/reference/cli/*.md` (deps, mcp, config, runtime, install, init, uninstall, update, compile, run, marketplace, lock, etc.) exists in the live CLI, and vice versa -- no orphaned or undocumented commands found among those inspected.
- **README.md cross-reference**: all commands and flags referenced in `README.md` (`apm install`, `apm install --mcp`, `apm marketplace add`, `apm compile -t copilot`, `apm lock export`, etc.) exist and behave as described. The `reference/cli-commands` link resolves via an Astro redirect to `reference/cli/install`, so it is not a broken/stale reference.
- **Flag semantics accuracy**: `--target` value lists, default values (e.g. `--parallel-downloads` default `4`, `mcp search --limit` default `10`, `mcp list --limit` default `20`), and precedence chains documented in `deps.md`, `install.md`, `mcp.md`, `config.md`, and `runtime.md` all matched live `--help` output exactly where compared.
- **Error handling**: `apm install --nonexistent-flag`, `apm deps info` (missing arg), `apm config set` (missing args), and `apm runtime setup badruntime` all exit with code `2` and print a clean `Usage:` + `Error:` message -- no raw Python tracebacks observed.
- **`-v/--verbose` and `-y/--yes` short-flag consistency**: every command offering these flags uses the same short letters (`-v`, `-y`) with only wording variations in the help description, which is expected and not flagged.
- **`--help` coverage**: every one of the 22 explicitly-required command/subcommand invocations plus spot checks (`apm search`, `apm find`, `apm marketplace`, `apm marketplace add`, `apm lock`) produced valid help text; no missing `--help` support anywhere.
